data.body:
Second remediation pass (2026-08-21, worktree at origin/main `960fbfef2f`). All citations
re-verified against that tree and updated — the previous set was computed against an older HEAD and
had drifted (`content_triggered_overlays` is `registry.py:461`, not `:416`;
`glob_triggered_overlays` `:340`, not `:295`; `project_trigger_extensions` `:299`, not `:254`;
`code-review.yaml:63`/`:116`/`:120`, not `:64`/`:118`).

What the rv9 review blocked, and what changed:

1. E1/E6/E2 + A1 — "or a new conditional branch" was undefined and unexercised by any cited corpus
   case. DROPPED. The detector is now added DECLARATIONS only, and the plan says so explicitly with
   the deferral recorded. Every SELECT/NOT-SELECT case in the corpus is a declaration shape, so the
   detector's scope now matches its calibration exactly.

2. T8 — guard (vii)'s "newly introduced vs pre-existing" narrowing gave the reviewer LLM no way to
   decide the distinction: the deterministic trigger signal is used for overlay SELECTION only and
   never reaches the prompt (`workflow_ops.py:61-65` supplies context/changed_files/scope_context).
   Rather than wire provenance through, the plan now specifies the prompt wording in terms the
   reviewer can decide from the diff it already has: newly introduced = implementing lines appear as
   ADDED (`+`) lines in the diff under review; anything reachable only through unadded lines is
   pre-existing and stays advisory; a named violating input = a concrete value/argument/call
   sequence stated verbatim in the finding.

3. project.portability (blocking here) — the earlier draft keyed the detector on `src/**` plus
   Python `def`/`class`, which is a layout-and-language assumption: for a Ruby (`lib/`), Java
   (`src/main/java`), Next.js (`app/`) or .NET target the trigger would silently never fire, and the
   overlay would stay unreachable there with no observable error. Removed both assumptions. The
   detector now reuses the EXISTING polyglot `_REMOVED_DECL_RE` (`registry.py:399-412`, already
   covering Go `func`, Rust `fn`, JS/TS `function`/arrow, `class`) applied to `+` lines, and its
   only path predicates are the committed `tests` globs plus a docs/data extension skip. It is an
   in-process text scan, so no CI provider is involved at all.

Detector design verified empirically before writing it down. The rule is: an added line matching
`_REMOVED_DECL_RE` whose DECLARED NAME is not also removed on a `-` line in the SAME file, and no
changed file under the `tests` globs. Replayed against all five cited commits in this checkout, that
rule reproduces every claimed verdict:
  d9e0f0e733 SELECT (git_adapter.py, 15)   721cb7d6ac SELECT (gitutil.py, 3)
  1c2bf6e57b SELECT (_lib_identity 9 + _lib_mutations 13 = 22)
  83d91d488c no-select   24917e843b no-select
The name-based (not text-based) comparison is load-bearing: 1703 (`83d91d488c`) re-wraps several
signatures across lines while adding annotations, so `+def resolve_event_commit(` does not
line-match the removed one-line signature — only the NAME matches. Counts re-checked directly:
`git show <sha> -- 'src/*' | grep -cE '^\+\s*(async +)?(def|class) '` gives 15 / 3 / 22 / 8 / 0,
matching the plan.

Also corrected: the pinning-suite count. `test_code_review_triggers.py` +
`test_code_review_deletion_impact.py` is 35 tests, not 46 (`test_code_review_evals.py` adds 23, so
58 across all three — that figure was right). Description is 7800 chars, under the 8000 admission
cap.
